_comment: SLEEPI research group — seeded by pinned identifiers, supplied by the owner 2026-08-06.
WHY THIS LIST IS PINNED RATHER THAN SEARCHED. Verified against the live
E-utilities API on 2026-08-05 and re-checked on 2026-08-06: `SLEEPI[au]`,
`SLEEPI[cn]`, `SLEEPI[ir]` and `"SLEEPI"[author]` all return 0. The reason is in
the records themselves — the group's articles carry no `CollectiveName` and no
`Investigator` entries, so there is no field for an author query to match. Nothing
is wrong with the queries; there is nothing yet for them to find.
A free-text `SLEEPI` search returns 5 records, none of them this group's — they are
matches on the unrelated SLEEP-I trial and on incidental text. Not a usable seed,
and a standing reminder that an acronym is not an identifier.
So this list is pinned. Pinned records are confirmed outright: they reach the
published list and the embed with no review step. To add a paper, add its
"pmid:…" or "doi:…" here. New work is NOT picked up automatically — that is the
cost of pinning. To get automatic updates as well, add the members' ORCID iDs
under `seeds.orcid`; the two combine, and the seed time windows and the freeze
action exist to keep departed members' later work out.
WHAT TO SWITCH TO ONCE THE JOURNALS START SUPPLYING GROUP AUTHORSHIP. The field to
watch is `[cn]`, NOT `[au]`. PubMed keeps a collective author in its own field,
which `[au]` does not search: measured on 2026-08-06, `"RECOVERY Collaborative
Group"[au]` returns 0 while `"RECOVERY Collaborative Group"[cn]` returns 18,
translated by PubMed as `[Author - Corporate]`. Re-check with:
esearch.fcgi?db=pubmed&term=%22SLEEPI%22%5Bcn%5D
The day that returns this group's records, replace the pins with:
"seeds": { "pubmed": [
{ "query": "\"SLEEPI\"[cn]", "label": "SLEEPI", "trust": "confirmed" }
`trust` IS THE PART THAT MATTERS AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL HERE. Only an `[auid]`
query is trusted automatically, because an ORCID iD is a unique identifier;
`[cn]` is a NAME, and this project has already seen the collision (SLEEP-I). So
without `"trust": "confirmed"` every hit arrives as a candidate, and under
`reviewPolicy: "strict"` a candidate is not in `publications` — the list renders
empty and stays empty on the embed for ever, because candidates are confirmed in
the wizard and an embedded page has no wizard. Setting it is an assertion that
`"SLEEPI"[cn]` returns this group's work and nobody else's: run the query and read
the results before writing it. If it ever brings in a stranger's paper, add that
record to `exclude` — exclude outranks everything, including this.
`trust` travels beside the query rather than inside it: `data-pubmed-trusted`
on the script snippet and `?pubmed-trusted=` on the iframe, holding the
zero-based positions of the trusted queries within `data-pubmed`. A flag
hidden in the query text could not be told apart from the search syntax. So
an embed of this list can carry everything inline; `data-list="sleepi"` is a
convenience for the maintainer's own pages, not a requirement.
WHAT NOT TO DO: putting these PMIDs into `seeds.pubmed` as `12345678[pmid]` terms
looks equivalent and is not. It is the same candidate trap described above, with
none of the benefit. The same identifiers in `include` simply work.
This `_comment` key is not part of ListConfig. `normalizeConfig()` in
src/core/config.ts rebuilds the config from known keys only, so it is ignored at
runtime and never reaches the rendered list.
